set.reason: Minor outer-sect disciple; renamed Tristram (male per source) in the remaster.
set.description: An outer-sect disciple of Misty Peak ranked around thirtieth, whom Zane defeats as a newcomer (Eps 81-107).

set.reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name per the adaptation's conventions.
set.description: A female Demon Night Clan Soul Sea master who fights alongside Lacey in the defense of the Heavenly Feather Sanctuary (Eps 943-949) and handles the aftermath with her (source ch 925).

A Saint of the Skyreach Sect who, with Saint Augustus, oversees sect justice and politics. A stern, scheming elder who clashes with Zane over the Julian Croft affair and later plots against him; Zane ultimately exposes his machinations. Male (source: Zhenren Tianqiong); the remaster corrected an earlier female portrayal.

set.issues: Source translation is pronoun-inconsistent for Aizen ('Lord Aizen'/'himself' but also feminine lines); remaster standardized male per the title evidence.
set.description: A Demon Night Clan warrior and descendant of a World Lord, encountered in the Illusion Battlefield arc (Eps ~1243-1271). A composed, calculating fighter who becomes an uneasy ally of Amber's circle. Male (source: Aizen). Distinct from the 'Arcane Aurora' light phenomenon of Eps 223-226.

A top Skytop Peak inner disciple and heavy-machete wielder known for the Reaper's Chop, his ultimate technique withheld until his three-move wager against Patrick (Eps 280-281). Proud, disciplined, shaped by three years of seclusion after early losses to personal disciples. Source: Xie Yun; the remaster merged an erroneous second render ('Shayna') back into him.

A short warrior-monk of The Hallowed Concord who joins Zane's party in the Illusion Battlefield halls arc (Eps 1273-1318). Fights with a hook and a borrowed Blade of Hallowed Censure, conceals the party in his Illusive Fog, and provides First Beacon guidance. Source: Jin Hai; the remaster merged an erroneous second render ('Jeffrey') back into him.

Champion of the Crystal Martial House and the Harlen Crown Prince's First-Tier fighter (Eps 787-845). Wields the famed saber Dragon's Tooth and later a Relic-grade spear; loses his arm to Logan in their second bout. Source: Zhan Yun; the remaster merged an erroneous second render ('Gregory') back into him.

The prodigy third son of House Sterling, known as 'Crazy Three' (source: Zhuge Feng). An arrogant rival who crosses Zane at the Capital auction and trials (Eps 58-126), later ambushes him with the Sevenfold Blade and is killed (Eps 169-176), triggering the Saints' judgment arc. The remaster merged an erroneous second render ('Frey') back into him.

The Queen of Punishment's devoted spearman (source: Mie), dispatched with Maren, Taryn, and Paige to hunt Lavender in the Dark World arc (Eps 1161-1172). Dies deliberately impaling himself on Lavender's Nightshard Spear; later mentions are retrospective. The remaster folded the stray 'Exterminator' label back into him.

set.reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name.
set.description: Vice leader of the Dragonblaze Hall (source: Nian Yang), encountered during the Upper World recruitment arc (Eps 447-448). The early-series uncle once also rendered 'Nolan' was unified under 'Bryson Lowell' in the remaster.

Zane's uncle, a House Lowell elder complicit in Bryson's usurpation (source: Luo Junyi). Announces Perrin's academy acceptance in the early arc and resurfaces during Zane's reckoning with the family (Eps 326-335) as Andrew's father. The remaster unified a late-arc second render ('Ken Lowell') back into him.

set.reason: Renamed from 'Elder Julian' in the remaster to resolve the collision with Julian Croft.
set.description: An elder of the Dragonblaze Hall (source: Zhao Zheng) who recruits promising cultivators for the Upper World (Eps 439-450).

set.reason: Renamed from 'Elder Shaw' in the remaster: 'Shaw' is reserved for the Dragon-blooded clan surname (source Feng), and this character is unrelated (source: Sect Master Xiao).
set.description: Leader of the Sea Wyrm Sect (source: Sect Master Xiao of the Fish Dragon Sect), prominent in the Sea Wyrm arc (Eps 687-773).

set.reason: Renamed from 'Master Jasper' in the remaster to resolve the collision with Jasper Reed.
set.description: A Skyreach Sect master and mentor figure during the tournament arcs (Eps 236-285). Source: Elder Xu of Tianyi Peak.

General Gavin, a commanding imperial officer in the Razorwing campaign (Eps 79-87), rugged and battle-worn. Always addressed with his 'General' title. The late-series son of Zane and Tia, formerly also named Gavin, was renamed 'Rory' in the remaster.

Lord Randy, prince of the Harlen Divine Kingdom (source: King Yan), a sharp-tongued royal fighter in the Harlen arc (Eps 783-928). The unrelated Duskfall Sect disciple formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Dermot' in the remaster.

set.reason: Renamed from 'York' in the remaster to resolve the collision with War King York.
set.description: A Sea Peak (source: Thick Sea Peak) opponent in the All Peaks Competition (Eps 238-243), wielder of the Mad-Monster Hacking technique (source: Tian You).

set.reason: The source rank (Battle Emperor) is rendered 'War King' throughout the remaster; York keeps the unified title.
set.description: The War King of the York Divine Kingdom (source: Battle Emperor Yu the Great), father figure of crown prince Fredrick, wielding dominion over the Great Yu lineage in the Divine Kingdoms arc.

The imperial army's field commander at Silverspire (Eps 131-140), a hammer-wielding veteran who leads the defense against the Dreadlords (source: Xing Tiansu). Prince Ray's double-pupiled fighter formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Sten' in the remaster.
Captain Shane, a military leader in the Razorwing campaign (Eps 63-79; source: Lu Xiao). The Tower of Sin seat-holder formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Garrick' in the remaster.
A House Sterling scion, Felix's brother (source: Zhuge Hong), hostile to Zane in the Capital arcs (Eps 44-126). The Seventh Prince formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Edmund' in the remaster.

Tristan Hayes (source: Xu Lie), an early antagonist who borrows the Indigo Blade from Julian Croft and falls to Zane (Eps 54-58). The young House Lowell member formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Barnaby' in the remaster.

A Cloud Hall disciple and Thunder Law adept (source: Zong Mo Xie) who defeats Edgar in the Martial Tournament (Eps 488-489). Chris Fane's nephew formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Petey' in the remaster.
See Finn Donovan. The Eagle Peak ring-wielder formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Boyd' in the remaster.

The reclusive top-ranked personal disciple of the Skyreach Sect (source: Li Yifeng), the only Sect's Chosen ranked above Patrick (Eps 280-367). The minor antagonist minion of Eps 40-49 formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Sid' in the remaster.

Elder Howard of Cloud Hall (source: Elder Wei), who mentors disciples through the obelisk trials (Eps 438-449). The Stormcrown Peak apprentice of Ep 118 formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Pim' in the remaster.
A fighter dispatched with Cassian, Maren, and Taryn in the Dark World arc (Eps 1161-1178). Felix's entourage member of Eps 99-101 formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Nessa' in the remaster.
Owen's girlfriend, a Violet-Core cultivator (Eps 760-765). Cora's maid of Eps 933-934 formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Tilly' in the remaster.
A Misty Peak pledge ranked sixteenth (Ep 80). Edmund's guard of Ep 349 formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Bram' in the remaster.
See Leo Brandt. The Ep 34-40 antagonist minion formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Burt' in the remaster.
A Skyreach Sect master of array work who trains Richard (Eps 246-257). The Sea Wyrm elder formerly sharing the name was renamed 'Master Croy' in the remaster.

Caleb Warrick of House Warrick (source: Wang Hengzhi), cowed by Zane in the early House arcs (Eps 30-91). The later characters formerly sharing the first name were renamed in the remaster (Pierce Preston, Rhett Garrett).
Jill's deceptively powerful small blade, used in the All Peaks Competition (Eps 235-272). The two unrelated swords formerly sharing the name were renamed in the remaster (Jade Saber, Verdant Edge).
Finn Donovan's blade at the All Peaks Competition (Ep 240). Zane's father's sword of Ep 19 was renamed 'Azurite Blade' in the remaster.

set.issues: 'Josh' (Eps 436, 447, 980) is this entity's human alias — same character, not a separate person.
'Celestial Paragon' survives ONLY as the Talent Tablet title (e.g. 'Golden Celestial Paragon'); as a race name it was unified to Demi-Immortal in the remaster.
Early-era tier name; Ep 185 bridges it in-world: 'Adept Realm was what warriors called those who had broken through the Nature Level.' Both are canon; do not retro-unify.
Carries the 'Shaw' surname coincidentally; he is NOT of the Dragon-blooded Shaw clan (source Feng) nor related to Yolande Shaw.
Carries the 'Shaw' surname coincidentally; not of the Dragon-blooded Shaw clan (source Feng) and unrelated to Liam Shaw.
'Shaw' is the show's deliberate surname for the source Feng clan (Dragon-blooded): Alexander, Victor, Hank, Brianna, Arnold Shaw are all clan members.
Zane Lowell's in-story pseudonym in the Upper World arcs — the same person, never a separate character.
The single canonical rank name (source 'Battle Emperor'); the remaster removed the parallel 'War Emperor' rendering.
